### What changed

1. **CleanSpark / Sandersville, Georgia — financing changed from proposed/priced to closed.** On September 25, CleanSpark disclosed the closing of **$2.276 billion** of 7.875% senior secured notes due 2031. Net proceeds are intended to finish the Sandersville facility, reimburse prior equity contributions, and fund debt-service reserves. Sandersville has a previously disclosed **175 MW critical-IT** lease; this is funded finished-capacity development on a controlled campus, not evidence that CleanSpark or its tenant wants an outside Georgia option. It strengthens Georgia M2 institutional-demand evidence while increasing competition for contractors, equipment and grid capacity. Sources: [September 25 SEC 8-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/827876/000119312526402944/clsk-20260925.htm), [July 14 lease 8-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/827876/000119312526302448/clsk-20260710.htm).

2. **ONE Nuclear — external-origination precedent and competitor/partner watch.** The September 23 business-combination closing created publicly traded ONE Nuclear Energy Inc. The company says it advances projects through site control, constraints analysis, regulatory planning and engineering coordination. Its Louisiana portfolio targets co-located generation and data-center campuses measured in hundreds of MW to GW, not the inference lane. September 28 local reporting adds that it used landowner LOIs before securing a hyperscaler, but also says the projects remain on paper, no reactor vendor has been selected, formal reviews have not begun, and roughly $180 million per project may be required to proceed. Earlier SEC disclosure described the company as development-stage, with nominal assets, no operating history or revenue and no project under construction. Treat this as a documented **outside-origination business model**, not buyer willingness to acquire Syncranicity options. Sources: [closing announcement](https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20260923848561/en/ONE-Nuclear-Energy-LLC-and-Hennessy-Capital-Investment-Corp.-VII-Announce-Closing-of-Business-Combination), [SEC risk disclosure](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1846416/000149315226022633/form10-q.htm), [September 28 reporting](https://www.nola.com/news/business/one-nuclear-louisiana-natural-gas/article_e8871c7c-cad0-44ac-85a4-3a3aeb7489a9.html).

## Buyer-match conclusion

No listing qualifies as a match to CleanSpark, Google, ONE Nuclear, Host Digital or another named operator. CleanSpark/Google evidence relates to controlled campuses or generation subscriptions; ONE Nuclear’s product is integrated generation and GW-scale campus development; Host Digital’s disclosed preference is 20–100 MW turnkey capacity with existing or near-term power. None of the 22 listings has parcel-specific written service, diverse fiber routes, acceptable cooling design, buyer acceptance or transferable control. Proximity, industrial zoning, existing three-phase service and advertised utilities remain V1 seller claims or proxies.

# Parcel-specific option business drafts

# Internal option-business drafts — Georgia intake, September 28, 2026

**Status:** internal proposals only. No seller received or accepted these terms. Amounts are modeled caps, not quotes or authority to spend. Georgia counsel must address option enforceability, recording, assignment/nominee rights, equitable-interest marketing/wholesaling disclosures, brokerage, tax, environmental access, securities and closing before any signature, payment or marketing.

## Shared business-term framework

- **Buyer/optionee:** a newly formed Syncranicity deal SPV, subject to entity/tax/counsel review.
- **Property:** exact title legal description and complete APN schedule; marketing acreage is not controlling.
- **Initial stage:** 60–90 days of paid exclusivity, seller data delivery and access; it may convert into the option only after exact parcel, owner authority, legal access and fatal desktop screens pass.
- **Option term:** 270 days after conversion, with two unilateral 90-day extensions. Longer timing should be requested where a utility study requires it.
- **Price:** advertised ask or a separately negotiated formula; no hidden markup representation. Any assignment economics and required disclosures are counsel-dependent.
- **Payments:** option/extension payments proposed as creditable to purchase price. Refund only for seller default, uncured title/authority failure, or a negotiated failure to deliver promised access/authorization; feasibility failure otherwise limits downside to paid consideration and approved restoration obligations.
- **Assignment:** express right to assign, nominate an affiliate/project buyer, transfer the SPV, and share diligence subject to confidentiality and law; seller consent cannot be unreasonably withheld if consent is required.

- **Seller cooperation:** written authority for planning, utility, water, fiber, title and consultant inquiries; delivery of existing surveys, studies, utility records, environmental files, leases and notices; reasonable signatures on nonbinding information requests.
- **Access:** desktop and nonintrusive access first; intrusive work only under a separately approved plan with insurance, indemnity, restoration and hazardous-material limits.
- **Conditions:** title/survey/access; zoning/use and no fatal moratorium; exact serving utility and studyable load path; water/cooling/wastewater; flood/wetlands/habitat/cultural/geotech/environmental; fiber-route feasibility; buyer/sponsor fit; financing; assignability and lawful marketing; no adverse change.
- **Title/cure:** preliminary title, recorded access/easements, lien/entity/authority review, objection and cure periods, termination/refund for uncured material defects.
- **Closing:** buyer-controlled conditions, no duty to close after a failed condition, casualty/condemnation protection, prorations and escrow/title closing.
- **Publicity/contact:** no buyer, seller or utility name/publicity without consent; no claim that the parcel is powered, entitled or buyer-backed.
- **Reliance/data:** seller makes no technical promises beyond negotiated representations; third-party reports should permit reliance/assignment to buyer, sponsor, lender and SPV when available.
